Lag.text: A Lagged Unit's next Movement costs +1 Action Point.

Deafen.text: A Deafened Unit's next Ability costs +1 Action Point.

Dazed.text: A Dazed Unit's next weapon attack costs +1 Action Point (body parts count as weapons).

Stun.text: A Single-Stunned Unit has -1 Action Point on its (next) Turn.

Single-Stun.text: A Single-Stunned Unit has -1 Action Point on its (next) Turn.

Double-Stun.text: A Double-Stunned Unit has -2 Action Point on its (next) Turn.

Triple-Stun.text: A Double-Stunned Unit has -3 Action Point on its (next) Turn.

Slow.text: A Slowed Unit has -50% Movement Speed until its next Movement.

Frail.text: A Frail Unit takes +50% Damage the next time it does.

Blind.text: A Blind Unit's next Damage/Heal Act deals -50% Damage/Healing.

Cripple.text: A Blind Unit's next Damage/Heal Act deals -100% Damage/Healing.

Silence.text: A Silenced Unit can't use Abilities.

Root.text: A Rooted Unit can't use Movement.

Exhaust.text: An Exhausted* Unit has -1 Action Point for each tier of Exhaustion. At Triple-Exhausted, the Unit dies.

Hard Terrain.text: Moving 1 meter through Hard Terrain takes 2 meters of Movement.

Feared.text: A Feared Unit can only do one Act on its turn (e.g. move, make one attack, use one Ability, etc).

Fumbling.text: A Fumbling Unit's next Act is completely negated (Movement, attack, spell, or anything that requires Actions).

Blinded.text: A Blinded Unit has -4 to all rolls.

Rooted.text: A Rooted Unit has can't move from its space (but it can attack, cast Spells, etc).

Stunned.text: A Stunned Unit skips its turn.

Cover.text: If a Unit has Cover from you (e.g. is behind an obstacle), everything you do to it gets -2.

DiceUpgrade.text: Having Dice Upgraded means, for example, d6's become d8's, or d10's become d12's. D12's and d20's just gain +1.

DiceUpgraded.text: Having Dice Upgraded means, for example, d6's become d8's, or d10's become d12's. D12's and d20's just gain +1.

DiceDowngrade.text: Having Dice Downgraded means, for example, d8's become d6's, or d10's become d8's. D2's and d20's just gain -1.

DiceDowngraded.text: Having Dice Downgraded means, for example, d8's become d6's, or d10's become d8's. D2's and d20's just gain -1.

LikeNormalTalents.text: like you would normally get extra Class Talents (e.g. with the extra Known Talents from Intelligence, if above 0)

Chainable.text: Chainable means only usable if your previous Act was the one mentioned.

Flank.text: Flanking is when you melee-attack an enemy, and an ally of yours is directly behind the enemy. As an optional rule (ask the QM), flank attacks can deal +1 Damage.

FoolsGold.text: Fool's Gold is an imaginary currency that can be converted to real Gold by spending 1 hour in a town or city. Fool's Gold lasts until converted to real Gold.

Heroic.text: This is your Heroic Class Ability and, after getting this Talent, you can no longer change your Talents inbetween Adventures.

WearShield.text: While wielding a shield, you can't use that hand for a weapon.

StatLimit.text: Your Stat limit is 2 and increases by 1 every 3 Levels (it's 2 at Level 1, 3 at Level 3, 4 at Level 6, 5 at Level 9).

SkillsRule.text:
Your Hero has Skills that can further add a bonus to your Checks!

Skills are like _tags_ your Hero has. Each Skill may give you a +1 to a Check, if it makes sense for that specific Check. You can add multiple Skills to the same Check, if it makes sense.
For example, let's say you want to remove a fallen tree from the road. Baseline, this would a Check with 2d6 + your {Might}. But if you have, say, the Lifting and Lumberjacking Skills, you can add +1 for each!

^However^, you may not add multiple Skills that overlap too much, by common sense! For example, if you have Legwork and Jumping, one could argue Legwork automatically includes Jumping, so you would not be able to add both to the same Check.
Also, the same Skill does not add with itself. Having the Jumping Skill twice does not increase your bonus.

^You have a number of Skills^ equal to your {Intelligence} + 2, and you can spend 3 Plot Points to get a new Skill.
^Important note:^ whenever you acquire a new Skill, it must be a ^one-word tag^ (unless it's from a special Ability or magic item)!

FlawsRule.text:
Flaws are just like Skills, but negative: one word tags that may give a -1 to a Check (e.g. Anxious, Injured, IBS). But there is an important distinction.
^Flaws are not automatically added to Checks.^ Instead, _you choose when to add a Flaw to a Check_ (for a -1).
If you added a Flaw and still succeeded, your team gets a Plot Point. If you failed, the Quest Master gets a Plot Point.

You can add as many Flaws as it makes sense to the Check and that many Plot Points will be produced.

^You have 3 Flaws^, and you may acquire more through Quirks (at the end of an Adventure), Abilities, or special situations.

_Note that it is in your advantage to have Flaws, so you have more opportunities to generate Plot Points!_
